title: Privacy-Preserving Age Verification & Identity — the technology and the actual code
author: research pass for the MELEK AI Witness (Hathor) knowledge corpus
source: Direct verification against the GitHub REST API, the npm registry, and HTTP HEAD/GET on every URL listed in `sources`. Star counts, licenses, archived status and last-pushed dates are as returned on 2026-09-05.
overview: How to prove a fact about a person — chiefly 'this person is over 18' — WITHOUT collecting or storing their documents. BRIEF.md sec.6 puts personal-info intake at signup out of scope and sec.7 keeps user private keys client-side; signup is email-only, no SMS. Everything below is ranked by that bias: privacy-preserving first, document-collection second. Nothing here is included unless the repository was fetched and confirmed to exist on 2026-09-05.

verification_method.how_repos_were_checked: `gh api repos/<owner>/<name>` returning full_name (post-redirect), license.spdx_id, pushed_at, stargazers_count and archived. Renames were followed: 0xPolygonID/js-sdk -> PrivadoID/js-sdk; gitcoinco/passport -> passportxyz/passport; google/identity-credential and openwallet-foundation-labs/identity-credential -> openwallet-foundation/multipaz; hyperledger/aries-framework-javascript -> openwallet-foundation/credo-ts; zk-passport/openpassport -> selfxyz/self; Consensys/linea-attestation-registry -> Consensys-Incorporated/linea-attestation-registry; privacy-scaling-explorations/anon-aadhaar -> anon-aadhaar/anon-aadhaar; privacy-scaling-explorations/zk-kit -> zk-kit/zk-kit.
verification_method.how_packages_were_checked: registry.npmjs.org metadata for latest version, declared license and publish date.
things_deliberately_left_out: Any repo that returned 404: holonym-foundation/zk-proofs, holonym-foundation/holonym-frontend, JMRTD/jmrtd (JMRTD is hosted on SourceForge, not GitHub), Proof-Of-Humanity/proof-of-humanity-contracts, sign-global/sign-protocol-evm, danielfett/sd-jwt-python. If it could not be confirmed it is not in this file.

The direct iso.org catalogue URL for ISO/IEC 18013-5 — iso.org returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients, so it could not be independently confirmed and is referenced by standard number only, via the EUDI ARF and openwallet-foundation/multipaz.
https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.IR.8525 returned 404 to a HEAD request; the NIST report is cited by its nvlpubs.nist.gov URL, which returned 200 and whose text was read directly.
archived_or_superseded_repos_flagged: zkpassport/zkpassport-sdk — ARCHIVED 2025-07-05. The live code is zkpassport/zkpassport-packages.
worldcoin/idkit-js — ARCHIVED 2026-04-14 (484 stars). Superseded by worldcoin/idkit.

how_this_repo_actually_gates_today.signup: `signup/server.mjs` exports `handler(req,res)` plus `validAccountName`, `readAccountActivity`, `computeProgress`, `stageCatalog`. There is no identity check of any kind at signup — verification is email-only per BRIEF.md sec.8, and account keys are generated client-side.
how_this_repo_actually_gates_today.closest_existing_guard: `signup/dev-trust-guard.mjs` — a startup/loopback guard around the dev-trust identity-assertion foot-gun. It is an auth safety rail, not an age gate.
how_this_repo_actually_gates_today.closest_existing_tier_ladder: `integrations/proof-of-human.mjs` already implements exactly the right SHAPE for this problem: a tier ladder (`anonymous` -> `device` -> `idme`) with a humanity score and an earnings multiplier, pure logic, no I/O, offline-testable. Its stated design principle is the operator's: 'we do NOT try to make spoofing impossible — we make it UNPROFITABLE.' An age gate should be a fourth signal on that same ladder (`ageAttested: true`), not a new subsystem.
how_this_repo_actually_gates_today.hathor_live: `site/hathor-live/server.mjs` is a single `handler(req,res)` router over /40hz, /reports, /practices, /api/chat. Any gate has to be a function called inside that router, in plain ESM, with an injectable fetch and an offline test — which rules out every Python and JVM option below as an in-process dependency.
house_style_constraints_that_eliminate_o: Plain ESM .mjs, no build step: eliminates circom/Noir/Rust proving toolchains from this repo (verification-only JS is fine).
Offline tests (injectable fetch, soft-fail-never-throw): any verifier that MUST reach a remote RPC needs its fetch injected and a soft-fail path.
No hosted backend of our own for keys: rules out running an issuer that would first have to learn a birthdate.

the_core_distinction.age_verification_vs_age_estimation: VERIFICATION derives a boolean from a signed government credential — the answer is right or the credential is invalid. ESTIMATION guesses from a face or from behaviour — the answer has an error distribution, and that distribution is not uniform across people. NIST IR 8525 keeps these strictly separate; so should any product copy.
the_core_distinction.why_over18_is_not_a_birthdate: The whole design win is that `age_over_18` is a BOOLEAN CLAIM, not a date. ISO/IEC 18013-5 mDL carries `age_over_NN` elements as first-class fields precisely so a bar or a website learns one bit. A birthdate is identifying; one bit is not.
the_three_leak_axes_to_judge_every_schem: What the RELYING PARTY learns (ideally: one boolean).
What the ISSUER / hosted service learns (that you verified, when, and often against whose domain).
What is LINKABLE across sessions and across sites (nullifiers, on-chain attestations, social graphs, biometric templates).

nfc_passport_reading_icao_9303.what_the_chip_is: An ICAO 9303 eMRTD is a contactless smartcard in the passport/ID booklet. It stores the printed data page as data groups (DG1 = MRZ text, DG2 = face image, sometimes DG3 fingerprints / DG4 iris) plus an SOD: a signed hash list over the data groups.
nfc_passport_reading_icao_9303.the_trust_chain: The SOD is signed by a Document Signer Certificate (DSC). The DSC is in turn signed by the issuing state's Country Signing CA (CSCA) master key. Verifying SOD -> DSC -> CSCA is 'passive authentication' and is what makes the chip's contents unforgeable. Confirmed in zkpassport/circuits README and selfxyz/self README.
nfc_passport_reading_icao_9303.access_control: You cannot read the chip without first proving you physically hold the book: BAC/PACE derives the session key from document number + date of birth + expiry date, all read off the printed MRZ. So the flow is always: camera scans the MRZ -> phone taps the chip over NFC.
nfc_passport_reading_icao_9303.what_the_zk_projects_do_with_it: They run the whole thing INSIDE the user's phone app, and the only thing that leaves the device is a zk-SNARK asserting a predicate over DG1 (e.g. dateOfBirth implies age >= 18) plus a proof that the SOD chain validates to a known CSCA root. The passport bytes never reach a server. This is the single most important architectural fact in this document.
nfc_passport_reading_icao_9303.certificate_distribution: Country public keys come from the ICAO PKD and from master lists published by individual states. selfxyz/self states it uses multiple ICAO member lists. (The ICAO PKD download host did not respond to an unauthenticated request on 2026-09-05, so treat master-list distribution as an operational task, not a URL.)
nfc_passport_reading_icao_9303.practical_coverage_caveat: Coverage is uneven. Countries use different signature algorithms, and each has to be supported by the circuit — see selfxyz/self's coverage map and av-lib-android-zkp-age-icao, whose circuit supports only RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 + SHA-256 DSCs with RSASSA-PSS SODs, RSA-4096 CSC and RSA-3072 DSC keys. A user whose passport is outside the supported set simply cannot prove.

eu_digital_identity_and_mdl.eudi_wallet: The EU Digital Identity Wallet reference implementation is fully open source under eu-digital-identity-wallet (verified: Android and iOS wallets EUPL-1.2; verifier endpoint, wallet core, PID issuer, OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP libraries Apache-2.0). The ARF repo (751 stars) is the normative architecture.
eu_digital_identity_and_mdl.the_age_verification_stopgap: Separately, the Commission published a white-label AGE VERIFICATION app (av-app-android-wallet-ui, EUPL-1.2, 296 stars, active 2026-09-04) with its own technical specification repo including 'Annex B - Zero Knowledge Proofs for the Age Verification Solution'. Its stated purpose is to bridge the gap under DSA Article 28 until EUDI wallets arrive at the end of 2026. This is the closest thing to an official, standards-track, non-commercial answer to 'gate by age without collecting documents'.
eu_digital_identity_and_mdl.mdl: ISO/IEC 18013-5 mobile driving licence carries `age_over_18` / `age_over_21` as discrete disclosable elements. The credible open implementation is openwallet-foundation/multipaz (Apache-2.0, 292 stars, formerly Google's identity-credential).
eu_digital_identity_and_mdl.credential_formats: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 (w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0) and SD-JWT VC (draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc) are the two formats in play; SD-JWT VC is what the EUDI stack uses for selective disclosure. OpenID4VCI issues them; OpenID4VP presents them.
eu_digital_identity_and_mdl.the_honest_catch: None of this helps a global crypto audience TODAY. Wallet rollout is member-state by member-state, non-EU users have nothing to present, and you cannot be the issuer. Build to OpenID4VP so you can accept these when they exist; do not wait for them.

proof_of_personhood_tradeoffs.blunt_summary: Personhood is not age. Every scheme in this category answers 'are you a unique human', and only World ID's newer Document credential touches age at all. If the requirement is an age gate, personhood systems are the wrong tool and importing one drags in their costs for none of the benefit.
proof_of_personhood_tradeoffs.biometric_collection: World ID's highest-assurance tier is an iris scan taken by a company-operated Orb — worldcoin/open-iris (MIT, 417 stars) is that pipeline, published by Worldcoin itself. Humanode requires recurring face biometrics. Both trade a permanent, unchangeable biometric for uniqueness. That bargain sits badly against a charter whose signup is deliberately email-only with no personal-info intake.
proof_of_personhood_tradeoffs.non_biometric_alternatives: BrightID (ISC, 244 stars) explicitly uses no biometrics — but substitutes your social graph, which is its own disclosure, and the repo has been quiet since 2025-10. Idena (LGPL-3.0) uses synchronised CAPTCHA ceremonies, which is a heavy recurring usability tax.
proof_of_personhood_tradeoffs.public_registry_warning: Proof of Humanity publishes a PUBLIC registry of humans with submitted video. Do not use it for anything privacy-shaped.
proof_of_personhood_tradeoffs.aggregation_warning: Human Passport (passportxyz/passport, AGPL-3.0, 1224 stars) works by AGGREGATING your accounts into one score. That is a linking machine. It is useful against sybils and actively harmful to unlinkability.

age_estimation_honest_numbers.the_authoritative_source: NIST IR 8525, 'Face Analysis Technology Evaluation: Age Estimation and Verification', Hanaoka, Ngan, Yang, Quinn, Hom & Grother, May 2024. Six commercial prototype algorithms against roughly eleven million photographs from four operational repositories (immigration visas, US arrest mugshots, border crossings, immigration office photos). Read directly from nvlpubs.nist.gov on 2026-09-05.
age_estimation_honest_numbers.nist_headline_finding_verbatim: 'accuracy is strongly influenced by algorithm, sex, image quality, region-of-birth, age itself, and interactions between those factors. There is no uniformly superior algorithm, and algorithm rankings differ across those factors.'
age_estimation_honest_numbers.mean_absolute_error: For the most accurate algorithm, MAE is about 3.5 years for a thirty year old (and 0.34 years for children under age 1 — accuracy is much better in young children than adults). Open-source models are worse: MiVOLO reports MAE 4.22-4.29 years face-only on IMDB-cleaned/UTKFace, 6.87 years from body alone.
age_estimation_honest_numbers.what_that_means_at_an_18_year_boundary: Because the error band is several years wide exactly where the decision is made, deployers use a 'Challenge-T' policy — auto-pass anyone estimated above T (e.g. 25), send everyone else to a real check. NIST Table 7, for an L=18 restriction on Application images, gives population-weighted FALSE POSITIVE rates (under-18s wrongly admitted) at T=25 of: incode-000 0.012 +/- 0.007, yoti-001 0.029 +/- 0.011, roc-000 0.030 +/- 0.011, dermalog-001 0.052 +/- 0.016, unissey-001 0.067 +/- 0.019, neurotechnology-000 0.220 +/- 0.029.
age_estimation_honest_numbers.the_cost_of_that: NIST Table 8 gives the matching FALSE NEGATIVE rates at T=25 — adults wrongly challenged: yoti-001 0.082, unissey-001 0.091, roc-000 0.099, neurotechnology-000 0.107, incode-000 0.120, dermalog-001 0.122. In plain terms: even a good commercial algorithm at a sensible threshold sends roughly 8-12 percent of legitimate adults to a fallback check. NIST: 'The two tables show the expected tradeoff between protecting young people and inconveniencing older subjects.'
age_estimation_honest_numbers.demographic_differentials: NIST Table 6 (Challenge-25 FPR for 17-year-olds by sex and region of birth) shows 'generally higher FPR in women than men, but with exceptions', and that 'The MAE values are also generally higher in women'. Rates also vary substantially by region of birth, with different algorithms best and worst in different regions.
age_estimation_honest_numbers.what_nist_did_not_test: The report explicitly excludes interactive sessions where a person can re-present to the camera, and does not measure disguises, cosmetics, or presentation attacks. So a face-estimation gate's real-world spoof resistance is UNMEASURED by this benchmark.
age_estimation_honest_numbers.conclusion_for_this_project: Face age estimation is the only option that needs no document and no third party — and it is the one that would require asking every user for their face, would run outside the repo's Node/ESM house style, would wrongly block roughly one adult in ten, and would do so unevenly by sex and region of birth. It is defensible only as a LOW-friction first filter with a real verification fallback, never as the sole gate, and never quietly.

self_hosted_kyc_reality_check.verdict: A self-hosted document-KYC stack is assemblable from open source — doctr or EasyOCR or Tesseract for OCR, InsightFace for face matching, Silent-Face-Anti-Spoofing for liveness — but assembling it means you now HOLD IDENTITY DOCUMENTS AND FACE IMAGES. That is the exact thing BRIEF.md sec.6 excludes, and it converts a repo with no personal data into a data-breach target with a retention policy, a DSAR obligation and a regulator.
self_hosted_kyc_reality_check.licensing_landmine: deepinsight/insightface has no repository-level LICENSE file and several of its models carry research/non-commercial terms. Check per-model before any commercial deployment.
self_hosted_kyc_reality_check.staleness_landmine: minivision-ai/Silent-Face-Anti-Spoofing has not been touched since 2023-10-03. Presentation attacks have not stood still.
self_hosted_kyc_reality_check.the_mrz_trap: OCR'ing a passport's MRZ is not verification. The MRZ is plain printed text — it can be retyped from any leaked scan. Only the NFC chip's signature chain proves the document is genuine.

crypto_gating_in_practice.what_front_ends_actually_do: In practice, DeFi front ends gate at the INTERFACE, not the protocol: IP-based geoblocking, terms-of-service click-through, wallet screening, and occasionally a signed attestation check. The contracts stay permissionless. Nothing in the on-chain layer usually knows anything about age.
crypto_gating_in_practice.the_attestation_pattern: The credible on-chain shape is: a trusted issuer signs an attestation carrying a FLAG and no identity, and the app gates on the flag. The reference deployment is Coinbase Verifications (MIT, live on Base) which issues EAS attestations meaning 'verified account' / 'verified country' with no identity in the payload. Ethereum Attestation Service (eas-contracts MIT, eas-sdk MIT) is the generic version and is trivially deployable to any EVM chain. Verax (Consensys-Incorporated/linea-attestation-registry, MIT) is the main alternative.
crypto_gating_in_practice.the_on_chain_privacy_problem: An on-chain attestation is a permanent, crawlable public record saying 'address 0x… was marked over-18 by issuer hathor at block N'. Anyone can enumerate the project's verified adults and correlate their subsequent on-chain behaviour. This is a genuine, often-ignored leak. EAS supports OFF-CHAIN attestations — EIP-712-signed payloads that never touch a chain — and for an age flag that is the correct default.
crypto_gating_in_practice.prana_evm_712217: PRANA is a standard EVM chain (chainId 712217, per PRANA_PAPER.md), so EAS, Verax, Semaphore verifiers, Anon Aadhaar contracts and snarkjs-generated Groth16 verifiers are all deployable there as-is. A `melek.over18` EAS schema on PRANA with Hathor as issuer is a few hours of work.
crypto_gating_in_practice.melek_graphene_reality: MELEK is a Graphene/Steem fork with NO smart contract VM, and CLAUDE.md restricts the Bot to standard ops only: comment, vote, transfer, delegate_vesting_shares, create_account_with_keys_delegated. There is no way to verify a SNARK on MELEK and no attestation primitive. The only on-chain expression of 'over 18' would be a post or memo by hathor naming the account — permanent, public, and maximally linkable, i.e. the worst possible privacy outcome. The MELEK-side flag must live OFF-CHAIN in the Bot's own store, keyed to the account name.
crypto_gating_in_practice.consequence_for_design: Do the proof off-chain in Node, store one boolean, and treat any on-chain attestation as an OPTIONAL, opt-in, PRANA-only convenience for people who want portability and accept the publicity.

ranked_by_time_to_ship.why_first: Its `verify()` runs LOCALLY in Node by default (`verifierMode: 'local'`), the API is a one-liner (`.gte('age', 18)`), and the whole integration is a browser QR plus a `handler(req,res)` that re-creates the query and verifies the posted proofs. That is exactly this repo's shape — no build step, no Python, no JVM.
ranked_by_time_to_ship.the_catch: The user must install ZKPassport's mobile app and own an NFC e-passport; the request travels over a websocket relay ZKPassport operates; and the project states it has had internal audits but NO external audit. The `uniqueIdentifier` de-duplicates accounts within your scope, which also means repeat visits are linkable within that scope.

ranked_by_time_to_ship.why_second: Same integration shape (`new DefaultConfigStore({ minimumAge: 18 })` + `SelfBackendVerifier.verify(...)`), a much larger project (1258 stars, active daily), and it additionally supports Aadhaar, which matters for an Indian audience. Run it as the SECOND accepted proof type behind the same internal boolean.
ranked_by_time_to_ship.the_catch: Verification checks a merkle root maintained in Self's contracts on CELO, so the verify path is not offline and needs an injectable fetch plus a soft-fail branch to satisfy the offline-test rule. The polished commercial path (`@selfxyz/enterprise-sdk`) is BUSL-1.1, not open source, and priced in credits — use the MIT `@selfxyz/core` path only. The per-scope nullifier carries the same linkability caveat.

ranked_by_time_to_ship.approach: An internal, off-chain `ageAttested` boolean on the existing proof-of-human tier ladder, optionally mirrored as an OFF-CHAIN EAS attestation, with an on-chain PRANA attestation strictly opt-in
ranked_by_time_to_ship.why_third: This is the piece that makes 1 and 2 useful and survivable. `integrations/proof-of-human.mjs` already has the tier/multiplier structure; adding an `ageAttested` signal is pure logic with an offline test and no new dependency. Storing the result as one boolean plus a nullifier hash means the repo still holds no documents, no birthdates and no names — which is the actual charter requirement.
ranked_by_time_to_ship.the_catch: It proves nothing on its own; it is a store for whatever 1 or 2 produced, so its integrity is only as good as the verifier feeding it. And if the operator ever wants the flag to be portable across the ecosystem, the on-chain EAS version publishes a crawlable list of verified adults — that trade must be the user's choice, not a default.

explicitly_not_recommended_as_the_primar: Face age estimation (MiVOLO/DeepFace) — wrong toolchain for this repo, and per NIST it wrongly challenges roughly 8-12 percent of adults with error that varies by sex and region of birth.
World ID — iris biometrics collected by a company-operated device; contradicts the no-personal-info-intake posture.
Self-hosted document KYC (OCR + face match) — turns a repo with no personal data into a document custodian.
Any scheme requiring us to be the credential ISSUER (Privado ID, digitalbazaar/vc) — being the issuer means first learning the birthdate you are then hiding.
recommended_paths_for_this_repo.build_to_this_interface: Accept SEVERAL proof types behind ONE internal boolean: `{ ageAttested: true, method: 'zkpassport'|'self'|'eudi-av'|'mdl', nullifier: <hash>, attestedAt: <iso> }`. Store nothing else. That way adding the EU AV app or an ISO 18013-5 mDL later is a new branch in one function, not a new subsystem — and no single vendor's outage or licence change can take the gate down.

privacy_failure_modes_summary.nullifier_linkability: Every ZK document scheme emits a stable per-(document, scope) identifier so you can prevent one passport creating many accounts. That same identifier links every session by that person within your scope. Mitigate by using a DIFFERENT scope string per surface, and by wrapping membership in Semaphore if you want the age check and later activity to be unlinkable.
privacy_failure_modes_summary.hosted_relay_metadata: Self and ZKPassport both route the request through infrastructure they operate. They learn that your domain asked someone for an 18+ proof, and when. They do not learn the passport.
privacy_failure_modes_summary.onchain_permanence: Anything written to PRANA or any EVM chain is permanent and crawlable. 'Verified adult' as a public on-chain label is a lasting disclosure about a person.
privacy_failure_modes_summary.graphene_permanence: The same, worse, on MELEK: a comment or memo is public forever and directly names the account.
privacy_failure_modes_summary.coverage_as_disclosure: If only some documents can prove, the ABILITY to prove is itself information (Anon Aadhaar implies Indian residency; a narrow circuit profile implies a specific issuing country's crypto).
privacy_failure_modes_summary.biometric_irrevocability: A leaked password is rotated; a leaked iris or face template is not. Any scheme whose enrolment is biometric is a permanent commitment on the user's behalf.
privacy_failure_modes_summary.social_graph_disclosure: BrightID substitutes 'who do you know' for 'what document do you hold'. For some users that is a larger disclosure, not a smaller one.

repos.name: selfxyz/self (Self, formerly OpenPassport / Proof of Passport)
repos.license: per-package (root LICENSE defers to each package; sdk/core is MIT; npm @selfxyz/core MIT; npm @selfxyz/enterprise-sdk is BUSL-1.1)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — the SDK is real and shipping, the mobile app + Celo registry are a live hosted dependency
repos.what_it_proves: From the NFC chip of an ICAO e-passport / biometric ID card, or an Indian Aadhaar QR: age >= N, nationality in/out of a set, OFAC-list non-membership, or bare personhood. Selective disclosure of individual DG1 fields is possible but optional.
repos.self_hostable: Verifier: YES. `@selfxyz/core` exports `SelfBackendVerifier`, a plain Node class you configure with `new DefaultConfigStore({ minimumAge: 18, ... })` and call as `verify(attestationId, proof, publicSignals, userContextData)`. It fits a `handler(req,res)` module directly. Issuer/wallet: NO — proofs are produced in the Self mobile app and the identity-commitment merkle root lives in Self's contracts on Celo, so the verify call is not offline.
repos.privacy_leaks: Returns a per-(scope, document) `nullifier`. That is deliberately stable: it de-duplicates accounts, and it therefore also links every visit by the same passport within your scope. Change the scope string and the link breaks across surfaces. The passport itself is never transmitted. The Self app and the Celo RPC you query can see verification timing. Aadhaar mode reveals you hold an Aadhaar, i.e. Indian residency.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA (EVM 712217): Solidity verifiers are in the monorepo `contracts/` and are deployable to any EVM chain, but the identity registry root they check is maintained on Celo, so a PRANA deployment needs a bridged/mirrored root. MELEK (Graphene/Steem fork): no VM — verify off-chain in Node and store the boolean in the Bot's own DB keyed to the account name.

repos.name: zkpassport/zkpassport-packages (ZKPassport SDK monorepo)
repos.license: no repo-level LICENSE file; the published npm packages @zkpassport/sdk and @zkpassport/ui are Apache-2.0 (v0.16.2, 2026-08-20)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — README states plainly: 'ZKPassport has undergone multiple internal audits, but it has not yet had an external audit.'
repos.what_it_proves: Same class as Self: from an ICAO e-passport / ID chip — `.gte('age', 18)`, `.in('nationality', EU_COUNTRIES)`, `.out('nationality', [...])`, `.disclose('firstname')`. Builder-style query API.
repos.self_hostable: Verifier: YES, and better than Self for this repo — `zkPassport.verify({proofs, originalQuery, queryResult, scope})` runs LOCALLY in Node by default and only falls back to ZKPassport's hosted verifier API if the local check fails; `verifierMode: 'local'` forces local-only. Wallet/prover: NO — the user proves in the ZKPassport mobile app, connected over a websocket relay ZKPassport runs.
repos.privacy_leaks: Returns a `uniqueIdentifier` bound to (document, your domain, your scope) — same de-dup/linkability tradeoff as Self. The relay sees that a request was made from your domain and when. README warns the browser-side result flag is tamperable; the proofs must be re-verified server-side against a re-created query.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA: an onchain certificate registry + registry SDK are in the monorepo (packages/registry-contracts, registry-sdk) — EVM-deployable. MELEK: off-chain only.

repos.name: zkpassport/circuits
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — Noir circuits, actively developed, unaudited externally
repos.what_it_proves: The circuit layer under ZKPassport: verifies the passport SOD signature chain (DSC signed by the issuing state's CSCA master key) inside a ZK proof, so only the derived predicate leaves the device.
repos.self_hostable: Yes as source, but proving needs the Noir/Barretenberg toolchain — heavy, not a fit for this repo's no-build-step rule.
repos.privacy_leaks: Circuit-level; the leak profile is whatever the query discloses.
repos.chain_fit: Proof verification contracts are EVM; MELEK cannot verify these on-chain.

repos.name: anon-aadhaar/anon-aadhaar
repos.maturity: usable-with-work, but going stale — no core release in ~21 months as of 2026-09
repos.what_it_proves: Ownership of a valid Indian Aadhaar (verifies the UIDAI government signature on the mAadhaar QR), revealing only chosen fields — age bracket, state, gender.
repos.self_hostable: Yes — circom circuits + JS SDK; proving runs client-side in the browser, verification runs in JS or in a Solidity verifier. No Aadhaar data reaches any server.
repos.privacy_leaks: Only serves Indian residents, so using it at all discloses Indian residency. The UIDAI signature is over a specific QR; nullifier design determines cross-app linkability.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA: `@anon-aadhaar/contracts` is EVM-deployable. MELEK: off-chain verify only.

repos.name: PrivadoID/js-sdk (formerly 0xPolygonID/js-sdk — Privado ID / Polygon ID)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — a full Iden3-based VC stack, considerably more machinery than a single age check needs
repos.what_it_proves: Nothing on its own — it is a wallet/verifier SDK for Iden3 verifiable credentials. Whatever an issuer signs (including 'birthdate < X') can be proven in ZK with selective disclosure.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, fully — issuer node, wallet SDK and verifier are all open source. But you must BE the issuer, i.e. you must first learn the birthdate you are then hiding. That collapses the 'no personal-info intake' property unless a third party issues.
repos.privacy_leaks: Depends entirely on issuer policy; revocation checks (RHS / on-chain state) can leak that a specific credential was presented.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA: Iden3 state contracts are EVM-deployable. MELEK: no.

repos.name: holonym-foundation/vole-zk-prover (Holonym / Human.tech)
repos.maturity: research-demo — a VOLE-in-the-head prover, explicitly 'not succinct'
repos.what_it_proves: Nothing by itself; it is proving machinery. Holonym's product proves government-ID or phone possession without revealing the document.
repos.self_hostable: Component is; the Holonym product is not — `holonym-foundation/id-server` (no license file, 1 star) is the service side and the flow depends on Holonym-run infrastructure.
repos.privacy_leaks: Holonym's flow historically routed the document through an issuer/enclave, so trust in their operator is required — that is a materially weaker property than Self/ZKPassport, where the document never leaves the phone.
repos.chain_fit: EVM contracts exist (`id-hub-contracts`, MIT, 2025-12-12). MELEK: no.

repos.name: rarimo/passport-zk-circuits (RariMe)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — circuits are real; the consumer surface is the RariMe mobile app
repos.what_it_proves: Same family as ZKPassport/Self: ZK proofs over an ICAO e-passport chip, including age thresholds.
repos.self_hostable: Circuits yes; the app + Rarimo's identity state chain, no.
repos.privacy_leaks: Registration writes an identity commitment to Rarimo's chain — a public, permanent record that some passport was enrolled at time T.
repos.chain_fit: Rarimo bridges state to EVM chains; PRANA would need that bridge. MELEK: no.

repos.name: zkemail/zk-email-verify
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — well maintained, real circuits, DKIM-dependent
repos.what_it_proves: That you received an email whose DKIM signature verifies against a given domain's public key, and that it matched a regex — e.g. 'this .edu / bank / government mail was sent to me' — without revealing the email body.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, fully — the whole point is that no server sees the mail. Needs circom + snarkjs to build; heavy toolchain, not a drop-in for this repo.
repos.privacy_leaks: Discloses the issuing domain and whatever the regex reveals. DKIM keys rotate, so proofs have a shelf life.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA: Solidity verifiers are EVM-deployable. MELEK: no. Note this repo's signup is already email-only, so zkEmail is the closest thing to an in-house fit if any age-bearing email exists — but ordinary mail does not attest age.

repos.name: semaphore-protocol/semaphore
repos.maturity: production-ready as a primitive (PSE-maintained, audited, widely deployed) — but it is a primitive, not an age system
repos.what_it_proves: Anonymous group membership + one signal per external nullifier. It proves 'I am in the set of people you admitted' without saying which one.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, completely — JS proving/verification, no hosted service. This is the piece you would use to STRIP the linkability that Self/ZKPassport nullifiers introduce.
repos.privacy_leaks: Leaks group membership and the size of the anonymity set. A small group is not anonymous.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA: EVM verifier contracts, deployable. MELEK: off-chain group management is fine — the Bot can hold the merkle tree itself.

repos.name: rozbb/zkcreds-rs (the zk-creds paper implementation, IEEE S&P 2023)
repos.maturity: research-demo — archived, academic artifact. Cite it, do not build on it.
repos.what_it_proves: Framework for anonymous credentials from existing identity documents (the paper demonstrates a passport-based flow).
repos.self_hostable: N/A — Rust research code.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A.

repos.name: AndyQ/NFCPassportReader
repos.maturity: production-ready for what it is — the reference Swift/iOS eMRTD reader; many products build on it
repos.what_it_proves: Nothing cryptographic on its own. It performs the ICAO 9303 chip session: derive the BAC/PACE key from the MRZ (document number + DOB + expiry, read off the printed machine-readable zone), then read DG1/DG2 and the SOD, and validate passive authentication.
repos.self_hostable: It is a client library — it runs entirely on the user's iPhone; nothing is hosted.
repos.privacy_leaks: Reads the FULL data page into the app's memory, including the photo (DG2). That is exactly the personal data BRIEF.md §6 keeps out — which is why the ZK projects run this step inside a phone app they control and emit only a proof. Do NOT build a web flow that ships DG1 to a server.

repos.name: tananaev/passport-reader
repos.license: no LICENSE file (all rights reserved by default)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — the best-known Android/Kotlin eMRTD reader; the missing license is a real blocker for reuse
repos.what_it_proves: Android-side equivalent of the above: NFC BAC/PACE session against an ICAO 9303 chip.
repos.self_hostable: Client-side library.
repos.privacy_leaks: Same as above — it hands your app the whole data page.

repos.name: ZeroPass/pymrtd
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — small, niche, but a genuine Python eMRTD/PKI implementation
repos.what_it_proves: Server-side parsing and passive-authentication verification of eMRTD data (SOD, DSC/CSCA certificate chain).
repos.self_hostable: Yes — pure Python, offline once you have the CSCA master list. Python, so out of this repo's ESM house style.
repos.privacy_leaks: If you run this server-side you are, by construction, receiving the passport data. That is the document-collection path, not the privacy-preserving one.

repos.name: li0ard/tsemrtd
repos.maturity: research-demo / early — tiny project, but it is the only TypeScript eMRTD parser found
repos.what_it_proves: TS/JS parsing of eMRTD data groups and the SOD.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, pure TS. Closest to house style of anything in this category — but 7 stars means you are the maintainer if it breaks.
repos.privacy_leaks: Same: it operates on the raw chip data.

repos.name: eu-digital-identity-wallet/av-app-android-wallet-ui (EU Age Verification white-label app)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — an official EU Commission reference implementation, actively developed, intended for member-state deployment; not a service you can call
repos.what_it_proves: A single 'is over 18' proof of age attestation, issued once from a national eID / e-passport and then presented to relying parties. Explicitly designed as the bridge until EUDI wallets land end-2026.
repos.self_hostable: The app is open source and so is the surrounding spec; the ISSUER side is a member-state function. You can run the verifier, you cannot be the issuer.
repos.privacy_leaks: Designed for unlinkability (batch-issued single-use tokens; see Annex B on ZKPs). Real-world leak surface is issuance: the issuer knows you obtained an age token.
repos.chain_fit: No chain. Pure OpenID4VP over HTTPS — which actually suits the MELEK/Graphene side better than any on-chain scheme.

repos.name: eu-digital-identity-wallet/av-doc-technical-specification
repos.maturity: production-ready as a SPECIFICATION — this is the document to copy if you design your own age flow
repos.what_it_proves: Defines the EU Age Verification profile, incl. Annex A (AV profile) and Annex B (zero-knowledge proofs for age verification). Grounded in DSA Article 28 (protection of minors).
repos.self_hostable: It is a spec.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A — but it documents the leak model you should be reasoning about.

repos.name: eu-digital-identity-wallet/av-lib-android-zkp-age-icao
repos.maturity: research-demo — the README itself says 'experimental'
repos.what_it_proves: ZK age proof derived from an ICAO e-passport chip, on Android.
repos.self_hostable: Source is open; the circuit only supports a narrow crypto profile (DSC = RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 + SHA-256, SOD = RSASSA-PSS + SHA-256, CSC RSA-4096, DSC RSA-3072, TBSCertificate 1600 bytes), so most of the world's passports will not verify.
repos.privacy_leaks: Same family as ZKPassport; the narrow profile also means the set of passports that CAN prove is small, which is itself identifying.

repos.name: eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-srv-verifier-endpoint
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — official EUDI reference verifier, Kotlin/Spring
repos.what_it_proves: Acts as an OpenID4VP 1.0 relying-party endpoint: initialise a presentation transaction, receive a `vp_token`, validate it.
repos.self_hostable: YES — that is its whole purpose. FLAG: Kotlin + JVM + Spring. That is a heavy toolchain and a second runtime next to this repo's plain Node ESM. Use it as a protocol reference, or run it as a sidecar behind a thin .mjs handler; do not port it.
repos.privacy_leaks: A verifier learns which claims it requested and that a valid wallet answered. With SD-JWT VC, unrequested claims stay hidden.

repos.name: eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-app-android-wallet-ui
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — reference wallet, not a shipped consumer product
repos.what_it_proves: Holds and presents PID and other EU attestations (mDL, age).
repos.self_hostable: Yes (it is an app you build).
repos.privacy_leaks: Wallet-side; issuer knows issuance.

repos.name: eu-digital-identity-wallet/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework (the ARF)
repos.maturity: production-ready as a specification
repos.what_it_proves: The normative architecture the whole EUDI ecosystem is built to, including which of ISO/IEC 18013-5 mDL, W3C VC and SD-JWT VC are used where.
repos.self_hostable: Spec.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A.

repos.name: openwallet-foundation/multipaz (formerly google/identity-credential — ISO 18013-5 mDL)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — the most credible open mDL implementation; originated at Google, now OpenWallet Foundation
repos.what_it_proves: ISO/IEC 18013-5 mobile driving licence: selective disclosure of licence elements including `age_over_18` / `age_over_21` as standalone boolean claims, over BLE/NFC proximity or ISO 18013-7 online.
repos.self_hostable: Yes — holder and reader are both in the repo and are Apache-2.0. FLAG: Kotlin Multiplatform / Android. Heavy toolchain relative to this repo.
repos.privacy_leaks: mDL's `age_over_NN` is the single cleanest primitive in this entire document: it is a boolean, not a birthdate. The residual leak is the device-signed session and, in some profiles, the issuer's ability to correlate if the reader phones home.
repos.chain_fit: No chain. Works equally well in front of a Graphene chain or an EVM one.

repos.name: openwallet-foundation/credo-ts (formerly Hyperledger Aries Framework JavaScript)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — mature-ish TypeScript VC framework with real deployments
repos.what_it_proves: Nothing by itself: it issues, holds and verifies W3C VCs / AnonCreds / SD-JWT VC over DIDComm and OpenID4VC.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, fully — and it is TypeScript/Node, which is the closest large VC stack to this repo's runtime.
repos.privacy_leaks: Depends on credential format. AnonCreds gives unlinkable presentations; plain JWT VCs do not.
repos.chain_fit: Ledger-agnostic; DID methods can be did:web (no chain at all), which is the right choice here.

repos.name: Sphereon-Opensource/OID4VC
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — TypeScript OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP libraries
repos.what_it_proves: Protocol plumbing for issuing and requesting verifiable credentials.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, Node/TS.
repos.privacy_leaks: Protocol-level only.

repos.name: digitalbazaar/vc
repos.maturity: production-ready for W3C VC Data Model issuance/verification in Node
repos.what_it_proves: Signs and verifies W3C Verifiable Credentials (Data Integrity proofs).
repos.self_hostable: Yes — pure Node. If Hathor ever issues its own 'over-18, checked by X' credential, this is the smallest honest way to do it.
repos.privacy_leaks: A plain VC is a bearer token with a signature; it is linkable unless you add BBS+/SD.

repos.name: openid/OpenID4VP (specification repository)
repos.maturity: production-ready specification (OpenID4VP 1.0 final)
repos.what_it_proves: How a website requests a credential presentation from a wallet.
repos.self_hostable: Spec.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A.

repos.name: worldcoin/idkit (World ID integration widget)
repos.last_active: 2026-09-04 (9 stars). Predecessor worldcoin/idkit-js (MIT, 484 stars) is ARCHIVED as of 2026-04-14.
repos.maturity: production-ready as software; the underlying scheme is the problem, not the code
repos.what_it_proves: Uniqueness ('one real human, once per app'), and — per docs.world.org — a Document credential that 'proves possession of a unique government document through NFC checks', described as useful for proof of age.
repos.self_hostable: NO in any meaningful sense. Requires the World App, and Orb verification requires physically visiting an Orb. Cloud verification of proofs goes to World's API or their on-chain router.
repos.privacy_leaks: The highest-assurance tier is IRIS BIOMETRY. World's own open-source `worldcoin/open-iris` is literally the 'Iris Recognition Inference System' the Orb runs. Proofs are claimed unlinkable across apps, but enrolment is a one-time biometric capture by a company-operated device — that is precisely the 'collect a permanent biometric' bargain this project's charter is trying to avoid. It has also drawn regulatory action in multiple jurisdictions. Do not ship this as the primary gate.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA: `worldcoin/world-id-contracts` (MIT, 2026-03-26) is EVM Solidity and deployable, but the merkle root of verified humans is World's, on their chains. MELEK: no.

repos.name: worldcoin/open-iris
repos.maturity: production-ready as an iris-recognition pipeline (it is what the Orb runs)
repos.what_it_proves: Nothing about age. Included here as the verifiable evidence of what World ID's top tier actually collects.
repos.self_hostable: Yes (Python).
repos.privacy_leaks: It IS the biometric collection.

repos.name: BrightID/BrightID
repos.maturity: usable-with-work, and losing momentum — no repo activity in ~11 months as of 2026-09
repos.what_it_proves: Social-graph uniqueness. Its README states: 'No personal data or biometrics are used for verification' — you are verified by a trusted group of close personal contacts plus a decentralized graph database.
repos.self_hostable: Node software is open; the graph is a network you join, not one you run.
repos.privacy_leaks: Your social graph position is the credential. That is a different, and for some users worse, disclosure than a passport check: it reveals who you know. Says nothing about age.
repos.chain_fit: Has EVM sponsorship contracts; MELEK: no.

repos.name: idena-network/idena-go
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — a live network, small
repos.what_it_proves: Personhood via synchronised 'flip' CAPTCHA ceremonies that all participants must solve at the same moment.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, it is a node you can run.
repos.privacy_leaks: Requires periodic synchronous participation — a hard usability tax. Says nothing about age.
repos.chain_fit: Its own chain. Neither PRANA nor MELEK.

repos.name: passportxyz/passport (Human Passport, formerly Gitcoin Passport)
repos.license: AGPL-3.0 (LICENSE file: 'Copyright (C) 2024 Passport XYZ Inc' + GNU AGPL v3)
repos.maturity: production-ready as a sybil-scoring product
repos.what_it_proves: An aggregate 'humanity score' from stamps (holding accounts, on-chain history, other credentials). Not an age proof.
repos.self_hostable: Source is AGPL and readable; the scoring API and stamp issuers are Passport XYZ services.
repos.privacy_leaks: Stamps aggregate your accounts into one profile — this is a LINKING system by design, the opposite of what an age gate should do.
repos.chain_fit: `passportxyz/eas-proxy` (AGPL-3.0, 2025-09-02) writes scores as EAS attestations on EVM chains — deployable to PRANA in principle. MELEK: no.

repos.name: Proof-Of-Humanity/proof-of-humanity-web
repos.maturity: usable-with-work; low activity
repos.what_it_proves: Registry membership as a unique human, arbitrated by Kleros disputes.
repos.self_hostable: Frontend yes; the registry is a public EVM contract.
repos.privacy_leaks: SEVERE for this use case: the registry is a PUBLIC list of humans with a video and a name/address. It is the least private option in this document. Not an age proof.
repos.chain_fit: EVM (Gnosis/Mainnet historically); technically PRANA-deployable, but do not.

repos.name: humanode-network/humanode
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — a live Substrate chain
repos.what_it_proves: One-human-one-node via periodic face biometric liveness.
repos.self_hostable: Node software yes; the biometric matcher is network infrastructure.
repos.privacy_leaks: Recurring face biometrics. Same objection as World ID. No age claim.

repos.name: WildChlamydia/MiVOLO
repos.license: Apache-2.0 (root LICENSE; note the README's './license' link 404s)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work as research code — do NOT treat its MAE as an age-verification guarantee
repos.what_it_proves: A numeric age ESTIMATE from a face (and optionally body) crop. Published in-repo results: MAE 4.22-4.29 yrs on IMDB-cleaned and UTKFace for face-only models; 6.87 yrs from body alone; the newer MiVOLO-Next line claims APPA-Real MAE 4.07.
repos.self_hostable: Yes — weights are on HuggingFace/Google Drive and inference is local. FLAG: PyTorch/Python. Completely outside this repo's plain-ESM, no-build-step, offline-test house style; it would need a separate Python service and a GPU or a slow CPU path.
repos.privacy_leaks: Requires a camera frame. Even if the frame is discarded immediately, you have asked every user for their face — a much bigger ask than 'do you have a passport'. Under-18s who look older pass; adults who look young are blocked. An MAE near 4 years around a hard 18-year boundary means a large error band exactly where the decision is made.

repos.name: serengil/deepface
repos.maturity: production-ready as a library; its age head is a weak, dated model
repos.what_it_proves: Face recognition + attribute analysis including an age estimate. Convenient, not accurate enough for a legal threshold.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, Python.
repos.privacy_leaks: Camera/photo capture; it is also a face RECOGNITION library, so the same pipeline can identify people — a serious scope hazard.

repos.name: yu4u/age-gender-estimation
repos.maturity: research-demo, unmaintained for ~5 years
repos.what_it_proves: Keras age/gender estimation from a face.
repos.self_hostable: Yes (Python/Keras).
repos.privacy_leaks: Camera capture; trained on IMDB-WIKI, which is heavily skewed toward white Western celebrities.

repos.name: shamangary/SSR-Net
repos.maturity: research-demo, abandoned — historical reference for compact on-device age regression only
repos.what_it_proves: Compact soft-stagewise age regression.
repos.self_hostable: Yes.
repos.privacy_leaks: Camera capture.

repos.name: dchen236/FairFace
repos.maturity: research-demo — but the most useful entry in this section for HONESTY, not for deployment
repos.what_it_proves: A race/gender/age-balanced face dataset and model, published specifically to measure demographic bias in face attribute models. Use it to test a candidate age model for bias before believing any vendor's headline number.
repos.self_hostable: Yes.
repos.privacy_leaks: It is a face dataset/model.

repos.name: paplhjak/Facial-Age-Estimation-Benchmark
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — an evaluation harness, not a product
repos.what_it_proves: Standardised comparison of facial age estimation methods across datasets. The right tool if you ever need to defend a chosen threshold.
repos.self_hostable: Yes.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A (benchmark).

repos.name: minivision-ai/Silent-Face-Anti-Spoofing
repos.maturity: usable-with-work; unmaintained since 2023 — presentation-attack techniques have moved on considerably since
repos.what_it_proves: Passive (no-challenge) liveness: is this a real face or a photo/screen replay.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, Python.
repos.privacy_leaks: Camera capture. And NIST IR 8525 explicitly does NOT measure presentation attacks, so pairing an old anti-spoof model with an age model gives you an unmeasured combined error rate.

repos.name: deepinsight/insightface
repos.license: no LICENSE file at repo root (per-model licensing; several models are research/non-commercial)
repos.maturity: production-ready code, but licensing must be checked per model before any commercial use
repos.what_it_proves: Face detection/alignment/recognition; the standard building block under most self-hosted KYC stacks.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, Python/ONNX.
repos.privacy_leaks: Face recognition — the strongest linking primitive in this whole document. Deploying it at signup would be the opposite of BRIEF.md §6.

repos.name: JaidedAI/EasyOCR
repos.maturity: production-ready for general OCR; not an ID-document parser on its own
repos.what_it_proves: Text extraction, 80+ languages. Would be the OCR layer of a self-hosted document-KYC stack.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, Python.
repos.privacy_leaks: Whatever document you feed it — this is the DOCUMENT-COLLECTION path. Only relevant if the operator explicitly decides to collect IDs.

repos.name: mindee/doctr
repos.maturity: production-ready OCR/document-understanding toolkit, actively maintained
repos.what_it_proves: Document text detection + recognition, from the company behind a commercial ID-parsing API.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, Python (PyTorch/TF).
repos.privacy_leaks: Same — you are holding ID images.

repos.name: tesseract-ocr/tesseract
repos.maturity: production-ready; the baseline OCR engine. Notably, its MRZ output on a passport data page is what a cheap 'ID check' actually is — and MRZ can be typed by hand from a leaked scan, so MRZ-only checks prove nothing.
repos.what_it_proves: Text from images.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, C++ binary.
repos.privacy_leaks: Document handling.

repos.name: ethereum-attestation-service/eas-contracts (EAS)
repos.maturity: production-ready — deployed across many EVM chains, simple and audited-by-usage
repos.what_it_proves: Nothing on its own. It is a generic registry: register a schema (e.g. `bool over18`), then have an issuer sign attestations against it, on-chain or off-chain ('delegated'/off-chain attestations are signed EIP-712 payloads that never touch a chain).
repos.self_hostable: YES, fully. MIT Solidity — deploy `SchemaRegistry.sol` + `EAS.sol` yourself. The npm `@ethereum-attestation-service/eas-sdk` (2.10.0, MIT, 2026-08-27) is plain JS.
repos.privacy_leaks: An ON-CHAIN attestation is a permanent public record linking an address to 'verified adult, at time T, by issuer hathor'. That is a real correlation surface: anyone can crawl it and build a list of the project's verified adults. OFF-CHAIN EAS attestations avoid this entirely and are the correct default here.
repos.chain_fit: PRANA (EVM 712217): directly deployable — this is the natural place for a `melek.over18` schema. MELEK (Graphene/Steem fork): NO smart contracts exist, and the permitted ops are comment/vote/transfer/delegate only; the only way to put an 'over 18' flag on MELEK would be a public post/memo by hathor naming the account, which is permanent, public, and maximally linkable. Keep the MELEK-side flag off-chain in the Bot's own store.

repos.name: ethereum-attestation-service/eas-sdk
repos.maturity: production-ready
repos.what_it_proves: Client for creating/reading EAS attestations, including off-chain signed ones.
repos.self_hostable: Yes — plain JS/TS, no hosted dependency beyond an RPC.
repos.privacy_leaks: Off-chain mode: none beyond who you hand the signed payload to. On-chain mode: public and permanent.

repos.name: Consensys-Incorporated/linea-attestation-registry (Verax)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — a real alternative attestation registry with modular verification hooks
repos.what_it_proves: Same category as EAS, with pluggable 'modules' that can enforce conditions at attestation time.
repos.self_hostable: Yes — MIT Solidity, deployable to any EVM chain.
repos.privacy_leaks: On-chain and public, same caveat as EAS.

repos.name: coinbase/verifications
repos.maturity: production-ready as a deployed pattern (live on Base), but the repo itself is quiet since 2024
repos.what_it_proves: The best real-world example of the shape you want: Coinbase issues EAS attestations on Base saying a wallet is 'verified account' or 'verified country', WITHOUT publishing who the person is. A dapp gates on the attestation, never on a document.
repos.self_hostable: The consuming contracts/SDK are MIT; the ISSUER is Coinbase and cannot be self-hosted. Read it as the reference architecture: trusted issuer + boolean attestation + public verification.
repos.privacy_leaks: On-chain attestations publicly mark addresses as KYC'd-by-Coinbase, which links a wallet to a real exchange account existing. Same crawlability objection.
repos.chain_fit: Base today; the pattern ports to PRANA one-for-one if Hathor is the issuer.

repos.name: tlsnotary/tlsn
repos.license: no SPDX license detected at repo root (crates carry their own terms — check before use)
repos.maturity: usable-with-work — well-funded (PSE), still pre-1.0 in practice

repos.chain_fit: EVM verifiers exist; PRANA-deployable. MELEK: no.

repos.name: zk-kit/zk-kit
repos.maturity: production-ready as a primitives library (PSE)
repos.what_it_proves: Reusable ZK building blocks (merkle trees, Poseidon, identity primitives) that Semaphore and friends sit on.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, JS/TS.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A.

repos.name: noir-lang/noir
repos.maturity: production-ready as a language/toolchain; the ecosystem around it is younger
repos.what_it_proves: The DSL ZKPassport's circuits are written in. Relevant only if you intend to write or audit circuits yourself.
repos.self_hostable: Yes. FLAG: Rust toolchain + Barretenberg backend — heavy; do not add to this repo.
repos.privacy_leaks: N/A.

repos.name: iden3/snarkjs
repos.maturity: production-ready as tooling — but note GPL-3.0, which matters if it were ever linked into distributed product code
repos.what_it_proves: Groth16/PLONK proving and verification in JS. Anon Aadhaar and most circom-based schemes verify through it.
repos.self_hostable: Yes, pure JS — verification can run in this repo's Node process with no network.
